questions.prompt: A vision model reports "9 bottles on the shelf". What should you do?

options.text: Count them yourself. The Claude and OpenAI docs both say counts may be approximate.
Accept it. Models count perfectly, so no check is needed for a shelf like this.
options.explanation: Both vendors' docs list counting as a limit.

options.text: Ask a second vision model and accept the majority answer of the two models.
options.explanation: Several models can share the same weakness. You can count by eye in seconds.

questions.prompt: You send an approved anchor and a new image to Claude. How should you set up the prompt?

options.text: Label the images "Image 1:" and "Image 2:", put them first, then list the checks.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's vision docs say to label each image and that Claude works best when images come before text.

options.text: Send the question first, then both images with no labels, in a random order. Put it all in one long message.
options.explanation: Without labels you can't refer to each image by name, and Anthropic prefers images before text.

options.text: Send only the new image and ask whether it looks right to you, in general.
options.explanation: Without the anchor and without criteria, the model has nothing to compare against.

questions.prompt: A logo on a package is tiny in the image. What helps a vision model read it?

options.text: Crop and enlarge that area and send it as its own image.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say to enlarge text, and the Claude docs say zooming in on regions improved results in Anthropic's tests.

options.text: Send the full image at a smaller size so it uploads faster.
options.explanation: Smaller images make small text harder to read, and the Claude docs warn about resized images.

options.text: Nothing. Vision models read any size perfectly.
options.explanation: Both vendors list small text or small images as a limit.
